currentContext.business: Incorporated on 27th January 1965 and registered at Rajapalayam, Virudhunagar (Tamil Nadu), the Company manufactures fibre cement boards, calcium silicate boards and insulation boards of vegetable fibre, straw or wood waste agglomerated with cement and other mineral binders, which accounted for 83.75% of turnover, and prepares and spins cotton fibre including blended cotton, which accounted for 13.40% of turnover; electric power generation from non-conventional sources (wind farm) contributed 0.13%. Products reach institutional and project clients, government bodies, infrastructure projects, builders and real estate developers, industrial and export buyers, contractors and applicators, architects and consultants, and retail consumers, largely through an extensive dealer and distributor network. Overseas building-products operations are run through the Sri Lankan subsidiaries Sri Ramco Lanka (Private) Limited and Sri Ramco Roofings Lanka (Private) Limited.

Building Products: HILUX LITE (light weight Calcium Silicate Tiles)
Ramco Power of Rain guard sheet
Insulation Boards of vegetable fibre, straw or wood waste
Ramco SmartBuild Tech Services (design, structural planning and technical consultancy)
Wind Power: Electric power generation using non-conventional sources (Wind Farm)

currentContext.expansion: The routed sections disclose no named capex project, capacity addition, commissioning timeline or plant expansion for the year. Capital expenditure is referenced only as a claim on cash in the Dividend Distribution Policy, which states that dividend decisions should be taken considering the Company's expansion/modernisation plans and investment in capital expenditure programmes. The only forward capacity-style statement is at product level: HILUX LITE (light weight Calcium Silicate Tiles), launched in the previous financial year, did a volume of around 1 lakh tiles and "can be scaled up to 2 lakhs plus tiles during 2026-27". Growth in the building products division is otherwise described as distribution-led - taluk-level dealer appointment, market-centre building and entry into newer geographical markets - rather than as new plant capacity. On the capital structure side, there were no changes in the nature of business during the year; paid-up capital rose only through allotment of equity shares on exercise of employee stock options, and Secured Redeemable Non-Convertible Debentures issued by private placement in February 2025 at a 7.60% coupon were partially redeemed on 06.02.2026 with the balance maturing on 07-02-2028.

risks.risk: Price competition from single-plant regional operators eroding realisation
risks.note: Management states that "Single plant Regional Operators" renewed their aggression and expanded into newer geographies, and that this impacted realisation in fibre cement sheets even as volumes grew around 6%.

risks.risk: Raw material cost and currency exposure
risks.note: Depreciation of the Rupee affected raw material cost during the year; the impact was only partially mitigated through consistent and judicious usage of raw materials and supplier negotiations. Sustainable supply chain is separately identified in the BRSR materiality table as a risk covering supply disruptions, raw material availability and cost volatility.

risks.risk: Cotton and yarn price volatility with weak demand for commodity counts
risks.note: Volatility in cotton prices continues with wide fluctuations in both cotton and yarn; India's 2025-26 crop fell 4% to 313 lakh bales on lower acreage and world production for 2026-27 is expected to decrease by 5%. The Company relies on shifting to value-added customized yarn counts to offset falling demand for commodity counts.

risks.risk: Geopolitical and fuel-supply disruption affecting demand phasing and substitutes
risks.note: Early signs of Middle East war tension were felt in the last quarter and created dealer up-stocking, while prices of substitutes inched up in Q4 due to an ongoing shortage of fuel; the macro review also flags geopolitical tensions, trade fragmentation and policy uncertainty as global downside risks.

risks.risk: Workforce health and safety in manufacturing operations
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR material issues table as a risk of workplace incidents in manufacturing operations, mitigated through strong EHS systems, training and compliance monitoring; the entity also commits to zero fatality targets and continuous reduction of LTIFR.

risks.risk: GHG emissions, energy cost and climate regulation
risks.note: Identified as both risk and opportunity, driven by increasing regulatory requirements and demand for low-carbon construction materials plus rising energy costs; mitigation is renewable energy, fuel switch to PNG and briquettes, carbon tracking, green product development and energy optimisation.
Flagged in the BRSR materiality table purely as a risk, with 100% recycling, reuse and monitoring systems as the stated mitigation.

risks.risk: Product quality, regulatory compliance and business ethics
risks.note: Failure to meet quality and regulatory standards may affect customer trust and market access, and non-compliance with regulatory or ethical standards may lead to reputational and financial risks; mitigated through robust quality systems, certifications, regular testing, internal controls and governance practices. Fair wages and labour practices are separately flagged, mitigated by labour-law compliance, audits and monitoring of contractor practices.

themes.title: Cement demand & pricing recovery
themes.need: Q1FY27 turned cement from a pricing story into a volume-share-plus-fuel-cost story. ULTRACEMCO grew domestic grey volume +13.1% YoY against an estimated ~7-8% industry, delivered its first Rs 5,000cr+ April-June EBITDA (Rs 5,146cr) with EBITDA/ton held above Rs 1,200, and crossed 200.1 MT domestic capacity a year early - but guided Q2FY27 cost UP ~Rs 130-140/ton and pinned the Rs 1,400/ton consolidated target to Q4FY28. The fuel shock, not price, is the swing factor: JKCEMENT's EBITDA/ton fell to Rs 982 from Rs 1,229 YoY despite +19% grey volume, DALBHARAT flagged pet coke 'surged to nearly $160/t' versus a pre-war $110-115, and NUVOCO defended INR 1,079/ton EBITDA only by cutting petcoke from 37% to 27% of fuel mix in a single quarter. Consolidation is visibly compounding (INDIACEM EBITDA/ton Rs 386->400->509->603 across four quarters; DALBHARAT closed Jaypee at Rs 2,850cr EV with Chunar operational and Rewa on trial within 50 days) even as DALBHARAT slipped its 75mt milestone from FY27 to FY28. SHREECEM/RAMCOCEM/JKLAKSHMI/JSWCEMENT/STARCEMENT/BIRLACORPN ride the same volume + consolidation axis.
themes.driver: Q2FY27 is the guided cost trough - ULTRACEMCO ~Rs 130-140/ton, JKCEMENT ~Rs 150/ton and BIRLACORPN Rs 70-80/ton of incremental cost; then fuel-mix agility (NUVOCO's petcoke swing) and whether DALBHARAT's ~Rs 150/t of procurement savings is really 'permanent, not timing'.

themes.title: Building-materials & home-improvement up-cycle
themes.need: The residential up-cycle pulls a broad finishing/home-improvement basket - tiles & sanitaryware (KAJARIACER/CERA/SOMANYCERA/ORIENTBELL/HINDWAREAP), wood-panels & laminates (CENTURYPLY/GREENPANEL/GREENLAM/RUSHIL/STYLAMIND), pipes/adhesives (PIDILITIND/SUPREMEIND/ASTRAL-tier) and paints (ASIANPAINT/CARYSIL/SIRCA). Premiumization + GST formalization shift share to organized players.
themes.driver: Festive/real-estate completion demand; GST 2.0 + commodity tailwinds; capacity commissioning and channel restocking.
